title: Talks, Attacks, and a Heist
gist: Partially paywalled 'The Adversarial' newsletter; the accessible text covers only Iran: after the U.S. midterms Washington must choose between patient blockade/sanctions pressure or renewed war (constrained by munitions shortages), while a hardened Tehran rejects a no-war, no-peace status quo but distrusts talks. Remaining sections (other adversaries, the 'heist') are behind the paywall.

insights.claim: With the U.S. midterms over, the next move in the U.S.–Iran impasse appears to rest with Washington, which may choose a patient approach of squeezing Iran's economy through the blockade and sanctions, reasoning Iran needs time to reconstitute its arsenal or advance its nuclear program.
insights.speaker: WOTR Staff
insights.so_what: Continued blockade/sanctions keeps Iranian supply constrained; watch for policy shift post-midterms.
insights.quote: In the short term, the ball appears to be in Washington’s court to determine the next move.
insights.locator: Now that the U.S. midterms are over

insights.claim: President Trump might see little to lose from a return to war with Iran and may believe a decisive defeat of Iran is still possible and could rebuild his political image.
insights.speaker: WOTR Staff
insights.so_what: Renewed U.S.–Iran hostilities remain a live tail risk for oil and Gulf shipping.
insights.quote: President Donald Trump might believe he has little to lose from a return to war.
insights.locator: Now that the U.S. midterms are over

insights.claim: A U.S. munitions shortage will be a practical constraint on any renewed war with Iran regardless of political intent.
insights.speaker: WOTR Staff
insights.so_what: Munitions depletion constrains escalation and supports defense production demand.
insights.quote: Regardless, a munitions shortage will be a practical constraint.
insights.locator: Now that the U.S. midterms are over

insights.claim: Iran's leaders call a no-war, no-peace status quo unacceptable; Tehran will wait to see what Washington does but not indefinitely.
insights.speaker: WOTR Staff
insights.so_what: Time-limited Iranian patience implies rising risk of renewed confrontation.
insights.quote: Iran’s leaders have been clear that a no-war, no-peace status quo is unacceptable.
insights.locator: Now that the U.S. midterms are over

insights.claim: Iran has some incentive to negotiate but distrusts that the U.S. and Israel would refrain from attacking during talks, and will demand substantial guarantees the Trump administration may be unwilling or unable to give.
insights.speaker: WOTR Staff
insights.so_what: Low odds of a quick diplomatic deal; sanctions relief unlikely near term.
insights.locator: Now that the U.S. midterms are over

insights.claim: Iran's leaders believe they can absorb more economic pain because years of predicted economic collapse never materialized, and the killing of the supreme leader and other top officials early in the war has hardened the regime.
insights.speaker: WOTR Staff
insights.so_what: Economic pressure alone may not force Iranian capitulation; don't bet on regime collapse.
insights.quote: Iran’s leaders believe they can absorb more economic pain, after years of regular predictions of economic collapse did not come to pass.
insights.locator: Now that the U.S. midterms are over
